paper_title: Shifting Long-Context LLMs Research from Input to Output
caption: Proportion of real-user demand: The aforementioned 2K range refers to the interval [2K, 4K), and similarly for the other ranges. Solid color fill for input demand, slash fill for output demand in the Wildchat dataset.
model_annotation: This bar chart illustrates the proportion of real-user demand for different token length ranges, distinguishing between input and output demands in the Wildchat dataset. The horizontal axis contains four groups corresponding to token length ranges: 2K, 4K, 8K, and 16K, while the vertical axis is labeled "Number" and uses a linear scale ranging from 0 to 120,000 with tick intervals of 20,000. Each group consists of a pair of bars — one with a solid color fill representing input demand and one with a diagonal slash (hatched) fill representing output demand. The legend identifies eight categories: 2K-Input (light yellow, solid), 2K-Output (light yellow, hatched), 4K-Input (salmon/orange, solid), 4K-Output (salmon/orange, hatched), 8K-Input (light blue, solid), 8K-Output (light blue, hatched), 16K-Input (purple, solid), and 16K-Output (purple, hatched). In the 2K group, the input bar reaches approximately 9,320 and the output bar reaches approximately 78,188. In the 4K group, the input bar has a value of approximately 3,784 while the output bar is the tallest in the entire chart at approximately 108,494. In the 8K group, the input bar reaches approximately 1,401 and the output bar approximately 17,865. In the 16K group, the input bar is the shortest overall at approximately 832 and the output bar reaches approximately 4,247. Across all four groups, the output bars are consistently and substantially taller than their corresponding input bars. The groups appear ordered by increasing token range from left to right, and the input values decrease monotonically from the 2K to the 16K group. Each bar is annotated with its exact numeric value displayed above it.
